facts.text: Robot SF registers the single-robot environment under the env id "robot" with RobotEnv as its class, and calls it the primary supported training/evaluation environment
RobotEnv is the Gymnasium environment facade and the public environment API for simulation episodes
The default DifferentialDriveSettings sets max_linear_speed 2.0, max_angular_speed 1.0, max_linear_accel 1.0 and max_angular_accel 1.0
The linear speed is clipped to min_linear_speed, which is 0.0 when allow_backwards is false
The action space is a Box over commanded linear and angular accelerations, with low [-max_linear_decel, -max_angular_accel] and high [max_linear_accel, max_angular_accel]
The robot observation space is a Box with low [min_linear_speed, -max_angular_speed] and high [max_linear_speed, max_angular_speed]: the linear and angular speed

Commanded accelerations are clipped to the acceleration bounds, integrated over the timestep, and the resulting speeds are clipped to min_linear_speed..max_linear_speed and -max_angular_speed..max_angular_speed
The default simulation timestep is time_per_step_in_secs 0.1 s and the default simulation duration is sim_time_in_secs 200.0 s
max_sim_steps is the ceiling of sim_time_limit divided by the timestep
A simulation step increments the timestep, adds the timestep to the elapsed time and sets is_timeout at max_sim_steps
is_terminal is true when the route is complete, the time limit expired or the robot collided with a pedestrian, obstacle or robot
RobotEnv.step returns (observation, reward, terminated, truncated, info) and always reports truncated False
RobotEnv.reset applies the seed through global_reset_seed and _apply_reset_seed and forwards seed and options to gymnasium Env.reset
The environment action space is the robot factory's action space, and its observation space is fused_sensor_space of the robot observation, a target sensor and a LiDAR sensor
The default LiDAR scanner has max_scan_dist 10.0 and num_rays 272
The fused observation space is a Dict of drive_state and rays Box members

determinism.notes: reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 fixes the initial pose and the kinematics are deterministic, so one implementation repeats a trajectory for the same seed and actions; this package's fake draws the pose with Python's random.Random, while upstream seeds Python and numpy through global_reset_seed (robot_sf/gym_env/env_util.py:63-84) and rebuilds the crowd from the seed (robot_sf/gym_env/robot_env.py:695-705), so a seed gives different trajectories on the two

gaps: kinematic unicycle model only: no social-force pedestrians, no obstacles, no contacts and no collision or route-completion terminal condition; the reward is 0 and only the simulated time limit terminates an episode

the observation is a reduced standing of the fused space: drive_state carries the two robot speeds and a target vector, and rays carries 8 constant ranges, while the real environment returns a Dict with 272 LiDAR rays by default (robot_sf/sensor/range_sensor.py:148) and a stacked target vector
the pose is integrated with a simple unicycle Euler step, not the wheel-speed odometry of DifferentialDriveMotion.move
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by timestep_ms only
no rendering, recording, telemetry, planner, sensor noise or snapshot/restore; no physical device is modelled and the model was never validated against one
the fake backend was never compared with the upstream environment (Robot SF was not importable where the gate ran), so trajectories can differ from upstream's numpy and PySocialForce streams

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the world state is kept and stays readable
